_doc: Shared monthly matters for Deeds (core/deed_choices.gd). Each: id, kinds (empty = all), season, title, text, options. An option: id, tag (safe, bold, frugal, ignore), label, cost (in quiet days of takings), say, mult and days (a spell of better or worse days), rep (the Deed's name, -5 to 5), risk {chance, say, mult, days, rep}. {deed} and the nouns below fill in for the kind of Deed. A Deed's own matters are in its file under asks.

asks.title: The inspector calls
asks.text: The council's food hygiene inspector is at the door of {deed} with a clipboard and the expression of someone who has seen worse and remembers all of it.

options.label: Close for a day and scrub it from top to bottom
options.say: Five out of five on the door by teatime. You can see your face in the counter, which is not entirely a compliment to your face.

options.label: Tidy up while the inspector looks round
options.say: A four, and a useful word about the drain.

risk.say: He finds the thing behind the fridge. A three on the door, a follow-up visit and a regular who reads such things.

options.label: Say you are busy and could he come back Tuesday
options.say: He comes back Tuesday, unamused, and so does the score.

asks.title: Prices up at the {supplier}
asks.text: The {supplier} has written to {deed}: prices are going up from the first. The letter says 'unprecedented' twice and 'sorry' not at all.

options.label: Pay it and keep the peace
options.say: You pay up. They send you a calendar. Relations are excellent.

options.label: Haggle, and mention you have seen other prices
options.say: They knock a little off and call you a hard bargainer, which you take as a compliment.

risk.say: The haggling goes badly. Deliveries become 'when we can'.

options.label: Find another {supplier} further off
options.say: A new supplier, forty minutes away and slightly cheaper. The first delivery is an adventure.

options.label: Pretend you did not see it
options.say: They stop answering the phone. The next delivery is short.

asks.title: A coach party
asks.text: Someone has rung to say a coach party of fifty will be passing through on Saturday and would {deed} 'be a bother'. They say it in the voice of people for whom it is always a bother.

options.label: Lay on a proper welcome
options.say: Fifty people, one photograph and a collection for the driver. They will talk about it all the way home.

options.label: Take them as they come
options.say: They come, they eat, they ask where the toilets are. A good day.

options.label: Offer a group price to get a second coach
options.say: A second coach, from a different town, and a rumour of a third.

risk.say: The second coach goes to a garden centre instead.

options.label: Say you will let them know
options.say: They never hear back, so they eat in a motorway services.

asks.title: A bad review
asks.text: Someone has written two paragraphs online about {deed}, and one of them is about the tea. It has been read, by the look of it, by everyone you have ever met.

options.label: Reply politely and fix what is fair
options.say: A calm reply, a small fix and a better score the next month.

options.label: Reply at length, with receipts
options.say: Your reply is shared far and wide, and for once kindly.

risk.say: Your reply is shared far and wide, and not kindly. It becomes a thing.

options.label: Offer the writer a free meal and hear them out
options.say: They come, they eat, they amend the review. A convert, with a notebook.

options.label: Ignore it, it will blow over
options.say: It does not blow over.

asks.title: A rise for the {staff}
asks.text: Your best {staff} at {deed} has had an offer from down the road, and has mentioned it in the way people mention things they want you to hear.

options.label: Match the offer
options.say: They stay, and they work as though the offer was a compliment.

options.label: Offer a share of the Saturday takings
options.say: They like the idea and they like the Saturdays even more.

options.label: Meet them halfway
options.say: They think about it for a week. They take the other job.

risk.say: They take the other job and send a postcard.

options.label: Say you cannot afford it
options.say: They go. The next one needs training.

asks.title: The local paper
asks.text: A reporter from the local paper would like to write about {deed}. They have said 'human interest' three times.

options.label: Give the full tour and a photograph
options.say: A full page and a front page photograph. Several regulars buy two copies.

risk.say: The photograph is not your best angle. It is also the front page.

options.label: Give a quote and a free sample
options.say: A neat paragraph and a better Saturday.

options.label: Say not today, thanks
options.say: They write about somebody else.

asks.title: A do in town
asks.text: There is a do in town on Saturday, with a band, bunting and the cheerful kind of crowd. {deed} could do very well out of it, with a bit of effort.

options.label: Open late and put on a special
options.say: A special, a queue and a tune that stays in your head for a week.

risk.say: Rained off. You are left with forty unsold specials and the tune.

options.label: Stay open a bit later than usual
options.say: A little later, a little busier, a little richer.

options.label: Keep to the usual hours
options.say: The band plays on without you.

asks.title: A word from a neighbour
asks.text: A neighbour has come to {deed} with a complaint, a cup of tea and a very long pause before the complaint.

options.label: Listen, apologise and put it right
options.say: You listen, you apologise, you move the bins. They leave with a biscuit and a better opinion of you.

options.label: Offer them something for their trouble
options.say: A small gift and a smaller argument.

risk.say: The gift is taken, the complaint is kept, and the whole street hears about it.

options.label: Stand your ground, politely
options.say: You are courteous and immovable. It works, or it seems to.

risk.say: It does not work. A letter goes to the council, which is worse than the complaint.

options.label: Say you will look into it
options.say: You do not look into it. They remember.

asks.title: A hard week's weather
asks.text: The forecast for the week ahead at {deed} is the sort that gets a name. The wireless sounds pleased about it, which is never a good sign.

options.label: Prepare properly and take it on the chin
options.say: Shutters, sandbags and a flask. It blows, it rains, and the damage is a dent.

options.label: Do the basics and hope
options.say: The basics hold for most of it.

options.label: Open anyway and make a feature of it
options.say: Everyone who braves the weather is rewarded with a free tea and a story.

risk.say: Nobody comes, and the umbrella goes over the wall.

options.label: Hope for the best
options.say: The forecast was right. It is always right when it is bad.

asks.title: Storm damage
asks.text: A winter storm has found the weak spot at {deed}. It is wet, mainly.

options.label: Get a proper tradesperson in
options.say: Done properly, with a bill that has a sense of occasion.

options.label: Patch it with what is to hand
options.say: The patch holds until the next shower.

risk.say: The patch does not hold. Neither do the takings.

options.label: Hope it dries out
options.say: It does not dry out. Customers notice, and so do the buckets.
